IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Representatives Haler, Hailey, Dunn, and McCune

Bill.BriefDescription: Permitting motor vehicles to be unattended when defrosting equipment is operating for certain conditions.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to unattended motor vehicles; and amending RCW46.61.600.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 46.61.600 and 1980 c 97 s 2 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) No person driving or in charge of a motor vehicle shall permitit to stand unattended without first stopping the engine, locking theignition, removing the key and effectively setting the brake thereonand, when standing upon any perceptible grade, turning the front wheelsto the curb or side of the highway. However, a person driving or incharge of a motor vehicle may permit it to stand unattended with theengine running, the ignition locked, the brake effectively set, and,when standing upon any perceptible grade, the front wheels turned tothe curb or side of the highway, if reasonably necessary to allowdefrosting equipment to remove ice, snow, or condensation from themotor vehicle. (2) The most recent driver of a motor vehicle which the driver hasleft standing unattended, who learns that the vehicle has become set in p. 1 HB 2866motion and has struck another vehicle or property, or has caused injuryto any person, shall comply with the requirements of: (a) RCW 46.52.010 if his vehicle strikes an unattended vehicle orproperty adjacent to a public highway; or (b) RCW 46.52.020 if his vehicle causes damage to an attendedvehicle or other property or injury to any person. (3) Any person failing to comply with subsection (2)(b) of thissection shall be subject to the sanctions set forth in RCW 46.52.020.
